evidence.paraphrase: Society has eliminated prisons, poverty, and war.
evidence.quote:
There were no prisons, no slums, no insane asylums, no cripples, no
poverty, no wars.

evidence.paraphrase: Disease and aging have been eliminated.
evidence.quote: All diseases were conquered. So was old age.

evidence.paraphrase: The national population is held fixed at forty million.
evidence.quote:
The population of the United States was stabilized at forty-million
souls.

evidence.paraphrase: Because aging is cured, death now only comes to those who volunteer for it.
evidence.quote: Death, barring accidents, was an adventure for volunteers.

evidence.paraphrase: The average lifespan is now extremely long, making 56 young.
evidence.quote:
Wehling was fifty-six, a mere stripling in a population whose average
age was one hundred and twenty-nine.

evidence.paraphrase: A government bureau operates voluntary termination gas chambers reachable by phone.
evidence.quote:
"To be or not to be" was the telephone number of the municipal gas
chambers of the Federal Bureau of Termination.

evidence.paraphrase: Law requires a volunteer death for each newborn to be allowed to live.
evidence.quote:
The law said that no newborn child could survive unless the parents of
the child could find someone who would volunteer to die. Triplets, if
they were all to live, called for three volunteers.

evidence.paraphrase: Hitz explains overcrowding as the rationale for population control.
evidence.quote:
Without population
control, human beings would now be packed on this surface of this old
planet like drupelets on a blackberry!

evidence.paraphrase: Hitz recounts a past crisis of water and food scarcity that scientists addressed.
evidence.quote:
In the year 2000," said Dr. Hitz, "before scientists stepped in and
laid down the law, there wasn't even enough drinking water to go around,
and nothing to eat but sea-weed

evidence.paraphrase: Uncontrolled population would have grown to extreme numbers.
evidence.quote:
Would you like to go back to the good old days, when the population of
the Earth was twenty billion--about to become forty billion, then eighty
billion, then one hundred and sixty billion?

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling emotionally resists giving up any of his children.
evidence.quote: "I want those kids," said Wehling quietly. "I want all three of them."

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling kills Dr. Hitz to create room for a child.
evidence.quote:
Wehling shot Dr. Hitz dead. "There's room for one--a great big one," he
said.

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling kills himself and others to allow his triplets to live.
evidence.quote: And then he shot himself, making room for all three of his children.

evidence.paraphrase: The painter contrasts the idealized mural with the true nature of life.
evidence.quote:
"You think this is my idea of what life really looks
like?"

evidence.paraphrase: The painter is so affected he abandons painting.
evidence.quote:
He knew that he would never paint again. He let his paintbrush fall to
the dropcloths below.

evidence.paraphrase: Euphemistic official term 'Ethical Suicide Studios' is used for the termination facilities.
evidence.quote:
He corrected
himself, gave the municipal gas chambers their official title, a title
no one ever used in conversation. "I should have said, 'Ethical Suicide
Studios,'"

evidence.paraphrase: Hitz frames population control as producing lasting peace and abundance.
evidence.quote:
Now
centuries of peace and plenty stretch before us as far as the
imagination cares to travel.
